description: AOML v2.1 Semantic Constraint Architecture. Minimal primitive core derived from Cross-Linguistic Compositional Analysis (CLCA) across 16 typologically unrelated languages. Separates primitive geometry (Layer 1: primary axes, meta-axes, core operators, levels), axis-internal semantic subregions (Layer 2), and empirical structural rules with validation habitats (Layer 3). Grounds the Universal Fallacy Architecture (UFA) without ontology inflation.

primary_axes.description: Answer: what kind of claim is being made? Each axis represents a distinct truth-claim kind with non-interchangeable validation requirements. Seven axes constitute the minimal set required to explain cross-linguistic contrast patterns in the truth domain.

VER.name: VERIDICAL
VER.description: Factual correspondence. Truth-value of propositions; correspondence between claim and state of affairs.

AUTH.name: AUTHENTICITY
AUTH.description: Genuine vs. counterfeit. Origin integrity of objects, documents, and artifacts.

SINC.name: SINCERITY
SINC.description: Honesty of intent. Inner alignment between stated and actual belief or intention. Virtue, not fact.

NORM.name: NORMATIVE
NORM.description: Moral, legal, or procedural rightness. Ought-claims. What should be the case rather than what is.

ESS.name: ESSENCE
ESS.description: Inherent nature. Fundamental, definitional, or necessary properties. What something is by its nature, not by observation or convention.

VERIF.name: VERIFICATION
VERIF.description: Evidential establishment. The process of proving or confirming a claim through appropriate evidence. Runs claim→world — structurally distinct from discovery (world→claim).

LIFE.name: LIFELIKENESS
LIFE.description: Representational fidelity. Constructed resemblance to reality; verisimilitude. How closely a made thing approximates what is real.

meta_axes.description: Answer: what is the claim's scalar or temporal position within a primary axis? Meta-axes modulate primary-axis claims. They do not constitute independent claim types and cannot substitute for their host axis in any inference step.

DEG.name: DEGREE
DEG.description: Magnitude modifier. Intensity, threshold, and comparison position of a claim on any primary axis. Ordinal in natural language: more/less, enough/too much, greater than. Structurally analogous to f'(x) — the rate of change of the primary-axis claim.
DEG.substitution_constraint: DEG[A] cannot substitute for A in any inference step. See Structural Rule R5.
DEG.empirical_status: Confirmed by both CLCA protocols (seeded and naive).

TEMP.name: TEMPORAL
TEMP.description: Position modifier. Order, direction, and persistence of a claim across time. Ordinal: before/after, already/not yet, earlier/later. Adds internal stratification: past, present, and future levels. Structurally analogous to the integral of the primary-axis claim over time.
TEMP.substitution_constraint: TEMP[A] cannot substitute for A in any inference step. Internal level crossing (past/present/future) without justification = UFA Type 4. See Structural Rule R6.
TEMP.empirical_status: PROVISIONAL. Emerged as D21 in CLCA-Revision (6 of 8 Set A languages). Did not surface in CLCA-1.1 global synthesis. Cross-architectural confirmation pending.

core_operators.description: Answer: what structural transformation or relation is being asserted? Seven operators constitute the minimal primitive basis. Operator licensing is conditioned by axis, target type, and polarity. Conditions are specified in Layer 3 Structural Rules.

ATTR.name: ATTRIBUTION
ATTR.description: Assign property. 'X is [axis]' — asserts a truth-kind property of a subject. Universally licensed across all primary axes.

CAUSE.name: CAUSATION
CAUSE.description: Bring about or destroy a state. 'Make X [axis]' or 'make X not-[axis]'. Licensing is polarity-conditioned and target-type-conditioned. Positive causation (CAUS+) and negative causation (CAUS−) are not separate operators but are licensed differently across axes and target types.

polarity_conditions.CAUS_positive: Licensed for factual targets (VER, NORM institutionally). Blocked for dispositional targets (SINC — universal block, Rule R1). Blocked for non-manufacturable ontological targets (AUTH positive pole — Rule R3, ESS — Rule R2).
polarity_conditions.CAUS_negative: Licensed for AUTH (forgery, destruction of authenticity — Rule R3). Blocked for dispositional targets (SINC). Generally more restricted than positive causation for truth-states.

BECOME.name: BECOMING
BECOME.description: Change of state. 'X becomes [axis]'. Directionally asymmetric across truth-domain axes: positive emergence is natural, negative emergence is marked or blocked in most languages.

polarity_conditions.positive: Natural and productive for most axes (become-true, become-real, become-just).
polarity_conditions.negative: Marked, dispreferred, or blocked in 14 of 16 languages. Negative states are conceptualized as degradation or corruption, not autonomous emergence. See Rule R4.

RESULT.name: RESULT
RESULT.description: State established. 'X proved to be / turned out to be [axis]'. Marks an achieved or discovered state. Primary realization pathway for revelation-type constructions.

ABSTR.name: ABSTRACTION
ABSTR.description: Nominalize concept. 'Truth / justice / authenticity' — converts an axis-property into a standalone abstract concept. Universally productive except where noted.

exceptions.LIFE: Blocked. Nominalization of lifelikeness universally blocked cross-linguistically (14:2 ratio across 16 languages).
exceptions.ESS: Marginal. Abstract nominalization of essence varies by language and construction.

STRAT.name: STRATIFICATION
STRAT.description: Layered distinction. 'Inner vs outer truth / surface vs deep sincerity'. Marks internal contrast within an axis. Universally attested across all 16 languages.

exceptions.AUTH: Restricted. Internal stratification less natural for material origin claims.
exceptions.SINC: Restricted. Surface/deep sincerity distinction exists but is less productive than other axes.

CONTR.name: CONTRAST
CONTR.description: Opposition. 'True vs false / genuine vs fake'. Marks binary opposition or differentiated contrast. Universally licensed. Violations of proper contrast = UFA Type 5 (Contrast Frame Collapse).

REVEAL.name: REVELATION
REVEAL.description: Disclosure of latent truth. 'X was revealed to be [axis]'. Presupposes a latent pre-existing state that was already true before disclosure.
REVEAL.empirical_basis: Emerged unprompted across 4 or more unrelated language families (Georgian, Korean, Turkish, Finnish) in both CLCA protocols. 15 of 16 languages show preference for revelatory constructions.
REVEAL.key_diagnostic: LIFE blocks REVEAL — constructed things cannot be revealed, only discovered. This confirms the presupposition is structural rather than stylistic. RESULT + STRAT cannot reconstruct this presupposition.
REVEAL.reason_for_provisional_status: Behaviorally strong and structurally distinct from RESULT + STRAT, but requires cross-architectural validation using non-Claude LLM families before confirmation as primitive.

levels.description: Answer: at what stratum is the claim operating? Four levels govern permissible inference across strata.

EMPIRICAL.description: Physical observation. Claims grounded in observable, testable states of the world.

CONVENTIONAL.description: Social and legal norms. Claims grounded in institutional or socially agreed standards.

FORMAL.description: Logical and mathematical. Claims grounded in logical or mathematical necessity.

ULTIMATE.description: Metaphysical and definitional. Claims grounded in fundamental or definitional necessity. Not falsifiable by empirical counter-example.
ULTIMATE.constraint: Level-crossing without explicit justification = UFA Type 4 Stratification Misalignment.

layer_2.description: Axis-internal semantic subregions. Stable lexical territories that recurred in CLCA data within each primary axis. These are not independent primitive axes — they do not require their own rows in the legality matrix. They live within the axis that generates them.

structural_rules.description: Empirical constraints discovered through CLCA that overlay the core legality matrix. These are not primitives — they are findings about how the geometry behaves under specific conditions. Each rule maps to one or more UFA violation types.

R1.name: Dispositional Causation Block
R1.description: Direct causation of dispositional character traits is structurally prohibited across all tested languages. Applies to SINC and all its subregions (reliability, faithfulness). CAUSE is not blocked generally — only for dispositional targets. Character traits are internally cultivated, not externally produced.
R1.empirical_basis: 16 of 16 languages. Fisher exact p < 1e-9. Both CLCA protocols independently. The strongest single empirical finding in the system.

R2.name: Essence Stability
R2.formal: CAUSE × ESS → blocked; BECOME × ESS → blocked
R2.description: Essential properties are intrinsic and non-manipulable. Neither external causation nor gradual transition applies to essence. Things have or lack essential properties — they do not acquire or lose them through process.
R2.empirical_basis: 15 of 16 languages for both CAUSE and BECOME blocking on the ESS axis.

R3.name: Authenticity Polarity Asymmetry
R3.formal: CAUSE(+) × AUTH → blocked; CAUSE(−) × AUTH → licensed
R3.description: Authenticity cannot be manufactured or externally created (CAUS+ blocked), but can be destroyed or forged (CAUS− licensed). This asymmetry is the primary empirical evidence for the ontological target-type class: ontological properties cannot be produced de novo externally, though they can be corrupted.
R3.empirical_basis: 10 of 11 languages for CAUS+ block; 8 of 11 for CAUS− license. Asymmetry consistent across language families.
R3.ufa_type: Type 2 — Operator Overextension (positive polarity applied beyond licensed scope)

R4.name: Positive Emergence Bias
R4.description: Positive emergence is natural and linguistically productive. Negative emergence is marked, dispreferred, or blocked in most languages — conceptualized as degradation or corruption rather than an autonomous developmental process. Aligns with privation theory: negative truth-states are absences, not destinations.
R4.empirical_basis: 14 of 16 languages show the asymmetry. Two exceptions (Yoruba and Indonesian) are analytic languages where the asymmetry manifests pragmatically rather than morphologically.
examples: 'the statement became false' — marked or blocked in most languages
R4.ufa_type: Type 2 — Operator Overextension (negative polarity applied beyond licensed scope)

R5.name: Degree Meta-Axis Substitution Prohibition
R5.formal: DEG[A] cannot substitute for A in any inference step
R5.description: The degree of a primary-axis claim cannot establish that the claim holds. DEG is ordinal — more/less, enough/too much. The derivative is not the function. This single rule explains a large class of classical fallacies.
examples: High probability (DEG[VER]) does not equal truth (VER) — Appeal to Probability
Very sincere-seeming (DEG[SINC]) does not equal veridical evidence (VER) — Appeal to Emotion
More popular (DEG[NORM]) does not equal more just (NORM) — Argumentum ad Populum

R6.name: Temporal Meta-Axis Substitution Prohibition
R6.formal: TEMP[A] cannot substitute for A; TEMP internal levels (past/present/future) cannot be crossed without justification
R6.description: Temporal position, recency, or historical precedence cannot validate a claim on its host primary axis without independent method. Internal level stratification adds an additional constraint: inference across past, present, and future levels requires explicit justification.
examples: More recent therefore better (TEMP[NORM] → NORM) — Appeal to Novelty
Past investment creates future obligation — Sunk Cost Fallacy
Applying present standards to judge past events — Presentism and Historian's Fallacy
R6.empirical_status: PROVISIONAL — TEMP meta-axis status confirmed in CLCA-Revision (D21, 6 of 8 Set A) but absent from CLCA-1.1 synthesis. Cross-architectural confirmation pending.

validation_habitats.description: Methods are validation habitats, not semantic axes. Each primary axis has default methods that license the claim type and inadmissible methods whose use constitutes a UFA Type 3 Verification Habitat Mismatch.

admissible_methods: varies by the type of claim being verified

target_type_classes.description: Cross-cutting structural partition over the primary-axis space. Governs differential operator licensing. The target-type ontology may be structurally prior to the operator licensing matrix — axes identify semantic territories but target types may determine what operators are legal.

FACTUAL.description: States of reality. Externally observable and, for some axes, externally producible.
FACTUAL.cause_licensing: Generally licensed, subject to polarity conditions (Rule R3 for AUTH).
FACTUAL.become_licensing: Positive emergence natural; negative biased (Rule R4).

EPISTEMIC.description: Knowledge and evidence states. Truth-values are discovered or revealed, not produced. VERIF runs claim→world; VER as a knowledge-state runs world→claim.
EPISTEMIC.cause_licensing: Restricted — can produce conditions for knowledge, not the knowledge state itself.
EPISTEMIC.become_licensing: Verification states are achieved, not gradually undergone.

DISPOSITIONAL.description: Stable inner tendencies of agents. Cultivated through practice and revealed through pattern of conduct. Not directly observable and not externally causable.
DISPOSITIONAL.cause_licensing: UNIVERSALLY BLOCKED (Rule R1, p < 1e-9, 16 of 16 languages).
DISPOSITIONAL.become_licensing: Marginal — character development is possible but internally driven, not a simple state transition.

target_type_classes.deep_hypothesis: The three strongest CLCA empirical findings — the dispositional causation block (R1), the positive emergence bias (R4), and the cross-linguistic preference for revelation constructions — may all be surface projections of a single deeper constraint: languages treat factual targets as externally producible, epistemic targets as discoverable or revealed, and dispositional targets as internally cultivated. If confirmed, the target-type ontology is structurally prior to the operator licensing matrix.

core_legality_matrix.description: Primitive legality layer. Default licensing status before polarity, target-type, and meta-axis conditions are applied. Polarity and target-type conditions are in Layer 3 Structural Rules. REVEAL excluded from core matrix due to provisional status.

legend.restricted: licensed under conditions specified in Layer 3 Structural Rules

core_legality_matrix.meta_axis_rule: DEG[A] and TEMP[A] inherit the operator licensing of their host axis A. Neither may substitute for A in any inference step (Rules R5, R6).
core_legality_matrix.provisional_operator_note: REVEAL is provisionally licensed for VER, AUTH, SINC, NORM, ESS, VERIF. Blocked for LIFE (key diagnostic). Excluded from core matrix pending cross-architectural validation.

ufa_mapping.description: Every constraint violation in this architecture maps to a UFA violation type. See companion document: UFA — Universal Fallacy Architecture.
ufa_mapping.type_1_axis_transfer_error: Substituting one primary axis for another in a claim or inference. The truth-kind of the claim is misrepresented.
ufa_mapping.type_2_operator_overextension: Applying an operator beyond its licensed scope for a given axis or target type. Covers: R1 (CAUSE × DISPOSITIONAL), R2 (CAUSE/BECOME × ESS), R3 (CAUSE(+) × AUTH), R4 (BECOME(−)), R5 (DEG[A] → A), R6 (TEMP[A] → A).
ufa_mapping.type_3_verification_habitat_mismatch: Using an inadmissible validation method for a claim's axis. See Layer 3 validation_habitats for axis-specific inadmissible methods and canonical violations.
ufa_mapping.type_4_stratification_misalignment: Unjustified level jump across EMPIRICAL, CONVENTIONAL, FORMAL, or ULTIMATE strata. Also generated by TEMP internal level crossing (past, present, future) without justification.
ufa_mapping.type_5_contrast_frame_collapse: False or collapsed opposition. Violations of CONTR operator legality — false dilemma, whataboutism, false equivalence.
